explanation: A polynomial's zeros are the x-values where its graph crosses the x-axis (where f(x) = 0). In factored form f(x) = a(x − r₁)(x − r₂)(x − r₃), the zeros are sitting right inside the parentheses — slide r₁, r₂, r₃ and the three colored crossings move with them. The dashed vertical sweep glides across the window so you can watch the curve dip to exactly zero each time it passes a root.
bullets: Set each factor to zero: x − rᵢ = 0 gives the zero x = rᵢ.
A degree-n polynomial has at most n real zeros (here up to 3).
In factored form the zeros are read off directly — no solving needed.
